invalid_operation: Reducing the expression by associativity or precedence before parenthesization (e.g., collapsing a leading product chain or treating a prefix like a-b as fixed) and then enumerating only the reduced expression.
observations: Both source questions ask for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of operands and binary operators, preserving order.
The shared interface gives operands (integers) and operators (one of +,-,*), with exactly len(operands)-1 operators.

The natural deterministic procedure is interval dynamic programming: for each contiguous subrange, compute the set of all achievable values by splitting at every operator position and combining left/right value sets.
The final answer is the cardinality of the set for the full range.

The failed attempts show a common error mode: they reduced subexpressions using associativity/precedence shortcuts (e.g., collapsing a leading product, or assuming 7-7 always yields 0) and then enumerated only a reduced expression, missing parenthesizations that interleave across the assumed boundary.
A correct DP over all splits avoids such invalid reductions and handles all Catalan-many parenthesizations implicitly.
Set sizes can grow, but with at most 8 operands the number of parenthesizations is C_7=429, so explicit set DP is small and exact with integer arithmetic.
procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): let n=len(operands), ops=operators. If n==1 return 1. Build dp[i][j] as a set of integers for subexpression operands[i..j]. Initialize dp[i][i]={operands[i]}. For length L from 2 to n, for i from 0 to n-L, j=i+L-1, initialize empty set. For each split k from i to j-1, let op=ops[k]; for each a in dp[i][k] and b in dp[k+1][j], compute a+b, a-b, or a*b according to op and add to dp[i][j]. After filling, return len(dp[0][n-1]). Use Python ints; no floating point. This directly counts distinct fully-parenthesized values preserving operand/operator order.
replacement_operation: Enumerate all binary-tree parenthesizations implicitly via interval DP over every split point, combining full value sets for left and right subranges with the operator at the split, then take the cardinality of the full-range set.
uncertainty: The DP is exact for the stated quantity. The only residual risk is performance if the interface were extended far beyond 8 operands, since set sizes can grow; within the given bounds it is negligible. No semantic routing or task-ID dependence is used.
